SILVER SPRING, Md., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Urban One, Inc. (NASDAQ: UONEK and UONE, referred to as, "Urban One," the "Company", "we", "our" and/or "us") today reported its results for the three months ended September 30, 2026. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net revenue was approximately $88.0 million, a decrease of 5.0% from the same period in 2025. The Company reported an operating loss of approximately $126.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to operating income of approximately $2.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Broadcast and digital operating income(1) was approximately $19.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of $0.5 million from the same period in 2025. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was approximately $119.2 million or $(26.39) per share (basic) for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net loss of $2.8 million or $(0.64)(a) per share (basic) for the same period in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA(2) was approximately $12.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $14.2 million for the same period in 2025.

Alfred C. Liggins, III, Urban One's CEO and President stated, "Market conditions in radio continued to adversely impact revenue in the third quarter. We were helped by net political revenue of over $0.8 million in the quarter and the acquisition of stations in our Dallas market, effective July 17th, which contributed an additional $1.9 million of net revenue in the quarter. Net political revenue for the full year is expected to be $8.8 million across all divisions. Weak demand in the Cable TV scatter market, shifted more inventory to the direct response category at lower rates in the third quarter. We saw an increase in local digital revenue in our radio markets, but large client attrition and suppressed rates in national direct digital revenue meant significant revenue declines in the overall digital segment. Revised Adjusted EBITDA(2) guide for 2026 is now $40.0 million given the realities of the current advertising marketplace. Management is hyper-focused on cost reductions heading into next year and has identified at least $20.0 million of annualized savings."

Dispositions and Acquisitions

On April 28, 2026, the Company entered into an agreement to acquire Service Broadcasting Group, LLC ("Service Broadcasting"), including radio stations KKDA and KRNB in Dallas, Texas for $22.0 million, of which $3.3 million was put in escrow. At the same time, the Company also entered into an agreement to sell radio station KZMJ from the Radio Broadcasting segment to Fuzion Dallas, LLC for $6.0 million. The transactions included the transfer of each station's FCC license and related assets and were subject to approval by the FCC and other customary closing conditions. All stations operated in their current format until the transaction received FCC approval and closed. FCC approval was obtained on June 23, 2026 and the Company completed the sale of KZMJ on July 6, 2026. The Company recognized a gain of $3.2 million on the KZMJ disposition in the third quarter of 2026.

FCC approval was obtained on June 26, 2026 for the Service Broadcasting acquisition. The acquisition, which was completed on July 17, 2026, did not meet the definition of a business, and accordingly was accounted for as an asset acquisition in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification No. 805, Business Combinations. The cost of the acquisition was $22.2 million, including transaction costs of $0.5 million, with the allocation to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed on a relative fair value basis. The intangibles relate to FCC licenses and lease contracts acquired. Under ASC 805-50, no goodwill is recognized. The operating results for Service Broadcasting are included in the condensed consolidated financial statements for the period beginning after the closing on July 17, 2026.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, we recognized approximately $88.0 million in net revenue compared to approximately $92.7 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. These amounts are net of agency commissions. We recognized approximately $36.7 million of revenue from our Radio Broadcasting segment during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $34.7 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of approximately $2.0 million. This increase was primarily driven by increased revenue from acquired stations and political campaigns, partially offset by weaker overall market demand from the national and local advertisers. We recognized approximately $5.1 million of revenue from our Reach Media segment during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $6.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of approximately $1.0 million. This decrease was primarily driven by lower demand and overall network audio market decline. We recognized approximately $9.6 million of revenue from our Digital segment during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $12.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of approximately $3.1 million. This decrease was primarily driven by reduced demand for diversity, equity and inclusion-focused spend and lower effective rates on campaigns. We recognized approximately $37.3 million of revenue from our Cable Television segment during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $39.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of approximately $2.5 million. This decrease was primarily driven by the churn of subscribers and lower advertising rates.

Operating expenses, excluding depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, and impairment of goodwill, intangible assets and long-lived assets, were approximately $78.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $83.7 million for the comparable period in 2025. Operating expenses were down by approximately 6.5%, driven mainly by non-recurring music license settlement costs recorded during the three months ended September 30, 2025. Decreases in revenue-related variable expenses such as traffic acquisition costs, commissions, marketing, affiliate station compensation and research related expenses were partially offset by increases across expense categories attributable to station acquisitions.

Impairment of goodwill, intangible assets and long-lived assets was approximately $128.9 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026. The Company recorded an impairment charge of approximately $62.5 million related to radio broadcasting licenses, $25.4 million related to the Radio Broadcasting reporting unit, and $40.9 million related to the Cable Television reporting unit during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

Depreciation and amortization expense was approximately $6.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $6.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of approximately $0.5 million. This increase is primarily driven by amortization of intangible assets acquired in the 2026 station acquisitions.

Interest expense was approximately $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $9.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of approximately $7.4 million. This decrease was due to lower overall debt balances outstanding and lower effective interest rates. The Company recognized interest expense using an effective interest rate of approximately 5.27% on the 2030 First Lien Notes, 0.15% on the 2031 Second Lien Notes, and 7.71% on the 2028 Notes for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The effective interest rates on the 2030 First Lien Notes and 2031 Second Lien Notes differ from the contractual interest payment primarily as a result of the accounting for these debt instruments under Accounting Standards Codification No. 470-60, Troubled Debt Restructurings by Debtors.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded a benefit from income taxes of approximately $6.3 million on the pre-tax loss of approximately $125.4 million resulting in an actual effective tax rate of 5.0%. For the three months ended September 30, 2025, we recorded a benefit from income taxes of approximately $1.1 million on pre-tax loss of approximately $3.9 million resulting in an actual effective tax rate of 28.4%. The Company paid income taxes of approximately $34 thousand and $72 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Other pertinent financial information includes capital expenditures of approximately $1.1 million and $3.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in capital expenditures is primarily driven by the prior-year build-out of a studio in the Indianapolis radio market.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026 the Company repurchased $0.2 million or 55,073 shares of its Class D Common Stock at an average price of $4.39 per share. During the three months ended September 30, 2025, the Company repurchased $0.3 million or 17,659 shares of its Class A Common Stock at an average price of $17.49 per share. During the three months ended September 30, 2025, the Company repurchased $0.5 million or 69,049 shares of its Class D Common Stock at an average price of $7.22 per share.

Jennifer Witz to Depart Following Over Two Decades of Strong Leadership

Anjali Sud Brings Extensive Digital Media, Streaming, Technology, and Advertising Experience to Guide the Company's Next Phase

NEW YORK, Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SiriusXM today announced that Anjali Sud has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, effective January 1, 2027. This appointment follows Jennifer Witz's decision to step down as CEO following almost two and a half decades at the Company. Witz will remain in an advisory role at the Company until the end of 2027.

Sud has served as an independent director on the SiriusXM Board of Directors since March 2025 and will remain a member of the Board of Directors following her appointment. She brings extensive experience in digital media, streaming, technology, and advertising-supported and subscription-based businesses, as well as a proven record of building leading entertainment platforms. She currently serves as Chief Executive Officer of Tubi, where she has led the Company's rapid expansion, growing its audience to more than 110 million monthly active users, scaling revenue, and driving profitable growth.

Greg Maffei, Chairman of the Board, said, "Anjali has built some of the most successful consumer entertainment platforms. In her previous roles, she scaled audiences, expanded platforms, and led businesses supported by both advertising and subscription models. As a member of our Board, she has intimate knowledge of our business and strategy. With her digital media experience, CEO-level success, and Board perspective, we are confident Anjali will hit the ground running and build on our momentum as we continue to execute against our objectives. We believe she will be an outstanding CEO for SiriusXM."

"I am honored to lead SiriusXM in its next chapter," said Sud. "Premium audio experiences will be more important than ever to the future of entertainment, and I believe SiriusXM can evolve to lead that future. Since joining the Board, I have gained a deeper appreciation for the Company's strengths and potential. I look forward to working with the team to execute with ambition and expand value for our subscribers, advertisers, artists, creators, talent, partners, and shareholders."

Maffei continued, "Jennifer has made extraordinary contributions to SiriusXM over her 25-year career, including nearly six years as CEO. Her efforts include expanding in-car penetration and 360L rollouts, solidifying its premium, content-led subscription business with record-high customer satisfaction and record-low churn, securing an exclusive advertising partnership with YouTube, and building one of the nation's leading podcast networks. SiriusXM is now generating its best core financial metrics in years, returning to revenue growth and generating near-record levels of free cash flow. Jennifer is leaving SiriusXM with a strong foundation, and we are grateful for her leadership."

"Leading SiriusXM has been the most meaningful experience of my career," said Witz. "I am particularly proud of what our team has accomplished in strengthening the subscriber experience, expanding our advertising business, and unlocking greater value across our broader portfolio. I firmly believe that SiriusXM is on a strong path and that now is the time for a transition. Anjali brings the perspective, leadership, and understanding of the business needed to guide the Company forward. While I will be leaving my role as CEO, I'll remain a lifelong subscriber and supporter of SiriusXM."

About Anjali Sud

Sud will join SiriusXM from Tubi, where she has served as Chief Executive Officer since 2023. Under her leadership, the business scaled to more than 110 million monthly active users, expanded globally, and established itself as a leading entertainment destination. Prior to Tubi, Sud served as CEO of Vimeo, where she took the company public and led its transformation into a profitable, global video platform with 300 million users. Before that, she held various positions in e-commerce, finance, and media at Amazon and Time Warner. Sud has served as an independent director on the SiriusXM Board of Directors since 2025. She also serves on the Board of Directors of Dolby Laboratories, Inc. and Change.org. She holds an undergraduate degree from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, and an MBA from Harvard Business School.

About Sirius XM Holdings Inc.

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, with a portfolio of audio businesses including its flagship subscription entertainment service SiriusXM; the ad-supported and premium music streaming services of Pandora; an expansive podcast network; and a complete ecosystem of advertising solutions through SiriusXM Media and AdsWizz. SiriusXM offers live, on-demand, and human-curated programming across music, talk, news, sports, and podcasts, and the company reaches approximately 255 million monthly listeners across its platforms. With deep automotive manufacturer relationships and unique spectrum assets, SiriusXM is built to reach listeners wherever they are. The company connects fans to the voices, creators, and moments they love - creating communities where listeners engage, participate, and belong. For more about SiriusXM, please go to: https://www.siriusxm.com/

GATINEAU, QC, Oct. 29, 2026 /CNW/ -- The CRTC is launching a free, downloadable music database that makes it easier for broadcasters, artists and the public to identify Canadian music.

For the first time, information that broadcasters use to identify Canadian music is available in one place. The database brings together information previously spread across several industry sources, making it easier for Canadian artists to be discovered and played across the country.

This will also help radio stations identify and promote music that counts toward their Canadian content requirements.

The initial release includes a large selection of popular Canadian songs. New releases and older songs will be added regularly to the database including additional French, Indigenous, and third-language music. As part of the initial phase, the CRTC welcomes feedback from users to help improve the database and ensure it continues to meet the needs of broadcasters, artists, and the public.

Commuting experiences vary across six Canadian markets, while 73% say time on the road would be worse without audio

TORONTO, Oct. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- For the second year in a row, SiriusXM surveyed drivers across the country to understand how their experiences are changing on the road, the regional realities shaping their journeys and the role audio plays along the way.

More than one third (37%) of Canadians say their time on the road has worsened over the past year. At the same time, as work schedules and daily routines continue to shift, changing when, why and how often Canadians are on the road, people are finding ways to make more of that time. Nearly half (47%) say their drive feels like time entirely their own, while 73% say their drive would be worse without audio.

"Canadians can't always control the traffic, distance or delays that come with being on the road, but they are able to manage how they spend that time," said Susan Simpson, Senior Director, Brand, Marketing and Communications, SiriusXM Canada. "This year's study shows the important role audio can play in that experience, and how it can help make time behind the wheel feel more enjoyable, meaningful and their own -- something SiriusXM is proud to deliver to drivers every day."

Where You Live Shapes How You Commute

The study reveals distinct commuting realities across Canadian cities:

  • Toronto drivers face some of the longest and most stressful journeys, with 27% driving for an hour or more and 48% describing the experience as stressful.
  • Vancouver drivers show that shorter drives don't always mean easier ones, with only 11% driving for an hour or more, yet 46% describing their commute as stressful.
  • Montreal drivers have a strong connection to audio, with 85% saying their time in the car would be worse without it and 31% saying audio is the part of their drive they value most.
  • Calgary commuters are most frustrated by other drivers, with 42% citing them as their top stressor, while more than half (54%) say their drive feels entirely their own.
  • Winnipeg commuters are feeling the impact of construction, with 23% citing road construction or closures as their top stressor.
  • Regina commuters report some of the most manageable journeys, with 57% travelling less than 30 minutes and 26% describing their drive as stressful.

SiriusXM has teamed up with Canadian recruiter and career expert Emily Durham (@emily.the.recruiter), whose work gives her a firsthand view into how workplace trends, hybrid schedules and changing routines are reshaping when, why and how Canadians commute.

"The way we work has changed, and so has the way we commute," said Emily Durham. "Being in the car isn't just about getting to and from the office anymore. Whether you're heading into work, dropping off the kids, going to an appointment or running errands, it can be a chance to reset and make that time feel like your own. Having something you genuinely enjoy listening to can completely change how that journey feels."

Audio Makes the Journey Better

The SiriusXM Canadian Commute study shows that audio continues to play an important role, particularly among younger Canadians. Among audio listeners aged 18–34, half (50%) say audio improves their mood, while nearly a third (32%) have looked forward to their drive because of something they planned to listen to.

SiriusXM gives Canadians the freedom to choose what they want from their drive, whether that's music to energize, news to stay informed, comedy to lighten the mood or something to help them unwind. With 425+ channels across talk, comedy, news, sports and more, plus ad free music, SiriusXM offers something for every drive, mood and moment.

The survey was conducted in English and French. For comparison purposes only, a probability sample of this size would carry a margin of error of ±2.8 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.

Urban One, Inc. (urban1.com), together with its subsidiaries, is the largest diversified media company that primarily targets Black Americans and urban consumers in the United States. The Company owns TV One, LLC (tvone.tv), a television network serving more than 30 million households, offering a broad range of original programming, classic series and movies designed to entertain, inform, and inspire a diverse audience of adult Black viewers. As of September 30, 2026, we owned and/or operated approximately 76 independently formatted, revenue producing broadcast stations (including 59 FM or AM stations, 15 HD stations, and the 2 low power television stations we operate) located in 13 of the most populous African American markets in the United States. Through Reach Media, Inc. (blackamericaweb.com), the Company operates syndicated programming including the Rickey Smiley Morning Show and the DL Hughley Show. In addition to its radio and television broadcast assets, Urban One owns iOne Digital (ionedigital.com), our wholly owned digital platform serving the African American community through social content, news, information, and entertainment websites, including its Cassius, Bossip, HipHopWired and MadameNoire digital platforms and brands. Through our national multimedia operations, we provide advertisers with a unique and powerful delivery mechanism to the African American and urban audiences.
